newsitem.title: USA: CenterPoint to get $130 mln credit line.
newsitem.headline: CenterPoint to get $130 mln credit line.

text.p: CenterPoint Properties Corp said Wednesday it has received commitments for the establishment of a $130 million unsecured credit facility, which will replace the company's existing secured lines.
Co-lead by First Chicago NBD and Lehman Brothers, other banks committed to participate in the facility are ABN LaSalle, Bank of America Illinois, Bank of Boston and NationsBank, CenterPoint said.

The three-year facility will begin at an initial interest rate of LIBOR plus 145 basis points, 13 basis points below the company's average borrowing cost on its existing secured credit lines, the company said.

"The establishment of this un-secured facility positions the company for an investment grade credit rating which will enhance the company's efficient access to low cost debt capital," chief financial officer Paul Fisher said in a news release. "In addition, the unsecured credit facility will permit the elimination of property specific mortgages, which significantly increases the company's flexibility to recycle capital into higher yielding investments through the advantageous disposition of properties from time to time."

CenterPoint, a real estate investment trust that develops industrial real estate, also said the City Council of Chicago passed Wednesday a resolution of preliminary approval for the use of up to $55 million of tax-exempt financing in connection with CenterPoint's previously announced O'Hare Express Center development on O'Hare Airport. When implemented, this financing will provide the company a savings of at lease 200 basis points over conventional financing costs, CenterPoint said.
